name: Fatigue severity scale
seoDesc: Fatigue severity scale: a free health calculator that walks you through 10 values, with the formula spelled out and a worked example.
summary: The Fatigue severity scale calculator takes the numbers you enter and reports fatigue Severity Score (FSS) immediately. It is free to use, needs no account, and shows the working rather than just the answer. It is built for an informed starting point to take to a clinician, not a diagnosis. Nothing is submitted anywhere: the arithmetic runs in the page you are looking at.

sections.title: How does the Fatigue severity scale calculator work?
sections.html:
The Fatigue severity scale calculator takes the values in the form, applies the relationship described below and reports fatigue Severity Score (FSS) in the results panel.

Working from the top of the form: you choose the option that describes your case (the exercise brings on my fatigue., the I am easily fatigued. and the fatigue interferes with my physical functioning.).

The arithmetic runs locally each time an input changes. The page knows which values you have given it and which it still has to derive, so the results panel is never stale.

sections.title: The formula behind the Fatigue severity scale calculator
sections.html:
One relationship drives the whole page:

Fatigue Severity Score (FSS)=((1 ÷ 9) × my motivation is lower when I am fatigued. + (1 ÷ 9) × exercise brings on my fatigue. + (1 ÷ 9) × I am easily fatigued. + (1 ÷ 9) × fatigue interferes with my physical functioning. + (1 ÷ 9) × fatigue causes frequent problems for me. + (1 ÷ 9) × my fatigue prevents sustained physical functioning. + (1 ÷ 9) × fatigue interferes with carrying out certain duties and responsibilities. + (1 ÷ 9) × fatigue is among my three most disabling symptoms. + (1 ÷ 9) × fatigue interferes with my work, family, or social life.)

Read it as an ordinary equation. Where a word appears instead of a letter, it is the label of one of the boxes in the form; where a function appears, it is the usual mathematical meaning of that function.

sections.title: What is a worked example?
sections.html:
Open the page and it is already filled in. With the values it starts from — My motivation is lower when I am fatigued. set to Strongly disagree, Exercise brings on my fatigue. set to Strongly disagree, I am easily fatigued. set to Strongly disagree and Fatigue interferes with my physical functioning. set to Strongly disagree — it reports Fatigue Severity Score (FSS) = 1.

Those are real numbers produced by the same engine that runs when you press Calculate, so you can change any single box afterwards and watch the answer move from this starting point.

  1. Enter the values listed above, matching the units each box asks for.
  2. Read off the result. Any field you leave empty is the one the calculator solves for.
  3. Sanity-check the number against the relationship: Fatigue Severity Score (FSS) = 1 should be roughly the size you expected from My motivation is lower when I am fatigued. set to Strongly disagree and Exercise brings on my fatigue. set to Strongly disagree.

sections.title: What does the result mean?
sections.html:
• A number, filled in as soon as the inputs allow it.

If a number looks wrong, check three things in this order: that the units match what you had in mind, that no drop-down is still on its default, and that the value you entered is on the same scale as the rest — a rate typed as 5 rather than 0.05 is the classic mistake. Those three account for almost every answer that is out by a factor.

sections.title: When should you use it?
sections.html:
The Fatigue severity scale calculator earns its place in the middle of a task, not instead of one. It is most useful when:

  • Preparing for an appointment so you can describe your numbers clearly
  • Tracking a measurement over time and understanding what changed
  • Deciding whether a reading is worth a second look

sections.title: How do you get a reliable answer?
sections.html:
• Round only at the end. The calculator carries full precision internally, so re-entering a value you already rounded is the fastest way to introduce drift.
  • If a result surprises you, look at the order of magnitude before the digits: a plausible number in the wrong unit looks more convincing than an implausible one, and is easier to miss.
  • Keep the units you enter consistent. Mixing centimetres into a field that expects metres is the single most common way to get an answer that is out by a factor of a hundred.
  • Compare two scenarios by changing the input that actually differs between them, and keep the rest fixed, so the difference you see is the difference you meant to test.

sections.title: What else is worth knowing?
sections.html:
• Answers that depend on a drop-down reflect the option you picked, not a range. Switching to a neighbouring option is the quickest way to see how much that factor matters.
  • Some options are backed by reference tables that ship with the page, so the values are fixed data rather than a live lookup.

faq.q: What does the Fatigue severity scale calculator work out?
faq.a: It returns fatigue Severity Score (FSS). Every field in the form feeds the same relationship: press Calculate once and changing any of them updates the result immediately, with no page reload.

faq.q: What do I need to enter to use the Fatigue severity scale calculator?
faq.a: The form asks for a few values, which is 9 fields in total. Each one is labelled with what it means and, where relevant, the unit it expects. Anything you leave blank is treated as the value to solve for.

faq.q: How much do the drop-down choices change the answer?
faq.a: There are several choices to make (9 in total), and each one selects a different case rather than scaling the result. Switching a single option and watching the result is the fastest way to see how much that choice is worth.

With the values the page starts from, the calculator reports Fatigue Severity Score (FSS) = 1. Treat that as a reference point rather than a recommendation: it exists so you can tell at a glance whether your own inputs are on the same scale.

faq.q: Is the Fatigue severity scale calculator free to use?
faq.a: Yes — no account, no sign-up and no limit on how many times you run it. The arithmetic happens in your browser, so the values you type are not sent anywhere.

faq.q: Do I have to fill in every box?
faq.a: Fill in the ones you know. The result boxes are computed from them, so you never enter a value the formula can derive — press Calculate and every result updates together.
